name: block_received
description: A block that completed reception on this validator or was abandoned and pruned.  A block gets a row if it received a shred marked as final in the slot, and received all shreds up to the final shred, or if it was incomplete but collected later during pruning. Tallies are best-effort: on equivocated slots, shreds shared between versions of the slot may merge or double count. Delivery is best-effort: rows travel a lossy telemetry link, so a block_completed row can arrive without its block_received row or vice versa.

block_id.description: Block identifier; with slot, the alternate join key to block_completed. For blocks that never completed reception (or were abandoned early), this can be the null hash.

parent_slot.description: Slot number of the block's parent. If unknown, this will be UINT64_MAX, and likely means that a block header could not be parsed for this slot.

parent_block_id.description: Block identifier of the block's parent. If unknown, this will be the null hash, and likely means that a block header could not be parsed for this slot.

cancelled.description: Whether the block was cancelled due to a notar version becoming known. These blocks will only get reported if they are eventually pruned, so if the root does not advance, they will not be reported.

cancelled_reason.description: The reason the block was no longer attempted to be repaired.

merkle_root_mismatch.description: Received two merkle roots for the same FEC set.

notarized_version.description: A verified version of the block became known.

verified_parent.description: A verified version of a verified block's parent became known.

parent_off_mismatch.description: A data shred's parent_off disagreed with the slot's other shreds or with its block header.

invalid_block_header.description: Shred 0 did not carry a valid block header.

slot_complete_mismatch.description: A data shred's slot complete flag disagreed with the slot's other shreds.

cancelled_time.description: When the block was cancelled. Only turbine versions are cancelled. Occurs when a votor-driven version of the slot arrives while this version's block id is still unknown, or for invalid turbine blocks. 0 if not cancelled.

notarized.description: Either reached SafeToNotar locally or attached to a NotarFallback or stronger cert, rather than being the version received over turbine. Always false for blocks this validator produced as leader. A slot can report both a notarized and a non-notarized version, on separate rows.

is_leader.description: Whether the block was produced as leader.

caught_up.description: Whether the validator considered itself caught up to the cluster when the row was emitted. False from boot until rotor/repair closes on the network tip (set immediately for genesis bootstrap); otherwise during regular operation is set to True if the highest slot the validator has received completely is no more than one leader window behind its view of the current cluster slot.

fec_set_count.description: Number of FEC sets in the block; for blocks that never completed reception, this could be 0 if the shred with the slot_complete flag never arrived.

first_shred_received_time.description: Network arrival at the shred tile of the block's first shred, stamped before signature verification. Leader blocks: when the first entry batch reached the shredding stage, before any network send.

last_shred_received_time.description: Network arrival of the shred that made the block contiguous; not necessarily the highest-numbered shred. Minus first_shred_received_time: reception duration, valid only when this is nonzero. Leader blocks: when the final entry batch reached the shredding stage. 0 if the block never became fully contiguous (pruned or abandoned mid-reception).

first_repair_request_time.description: First repair request for a specific missing shred (window or ShredForBlockId request); highest-shred, orphan, ParentAndFecCount and FecRoot requests do not stamp this, so it can be 0 while their request counts are not. 0 if no window or ShredForBlockId request was sent; always 0 for leader blocks.

last_repair_received_time.description: Network arrival at the shred tile of the last repair response matched to an outstanding specific-shred request; other responses do not stamp this. 0 if none was matched; always 0 for leader blocks.

first_meta_received_time.description: Network arrival at the rotor tile of the block's first verified getParentAndFecCount or FecRoot response, including a FecRoot answer for a FEC set already held. 0 if no verified metadata response was received.

turbine_shred_received.description: Shreds received over the network via turbine, plus repair deliveries whose provenance could not be verified (failed nonce) and coding shreds. Near 0 for leader blocks.

parity_shred_received.description: Parity (recovery) shreds received. Near 0 for leader blocks: only network echoes of the block's own parity shreds land here.

repair_shred_received.description: Shreds obtained from peers via repair; nonce-verified deliveries only. Re-fetched pieces count once per delivery. Always 0 for leader blocks.

recovered_shred_count.description: Shreds reconstructed locally from parity data. Always 0 for leader blocks, which produce rather than recover their shreds.

last_completed_fec_set_index.description: FEC set index of the last piece of the block to complete Reed-Solomon reconstruction, which with out-of-order repair need not be the block's final index. UINT32_MAX if no FEC set was completed.

slot_complete.description: Whether the shred marking the block complete was received, or it became known through a getParentAndFecCount request.

equivocation_detected_shred.description: Whether equivocating shreds were detected on this slot before any notarized version arrived.

repair_shred_responses_received.description: Repair responses matched to an outstanding specific-shred request. Shreds delivered by verified highest-shred and orphan responses count in repair_shred_received but are not matched here, so this can be 0 while repair_shred_received is not. Always 0 for leader blocks.

parent_fec_count_responses_received.description: Metadata responses matched to an outstanding getParentAndFecCount request that pass proof-check.

fec_root_responses_received.description: Metadata responses matched to an outstanding FecRoot request that pass proof-check.

repair_request_window_count.description: Repair requests for one specific missing shred, by index. Always 0 for leader blocks.

repair_request_highest_window_count.description: Repair requests for the highest-numbered shred a peer holds, used to learn the block's length. Highest-shred requests seeded at boot, before the block was tracked, bypass this counter. Always 0 for leader blocks.

repair_request_orphan_count.description: Repair requests for the block's ancestry when its parent is unknown; a response carries shreds from up to 11 ancestor blocks. Always 0 for leader blocks.

repair_request_shred_for_block_id_count.description: Alpenglow ShredForBlockId requests, analogous to legacy window requests. Asks a peer for a specific missing shred, addressed by the block id it belongs to. Always 0 before Alpenglow and for leader blocks.

repair_request_parent_fec_count.description: Alpenglow ParentAndFecCount requests, analogous to legacy orphan requests. Asks a peer for the block's parent and its FEC set count. Always 0 before Alpenglow and for leader blocks.

repair_request_fec_root_count.description: Alpenglow FecRoot requests. Asks a peer for the merkle root of the FEC set at a given index. Always 0 before Alpenglow and for leader blocks.

fec_sets.description: Per-FEC-set reception detail, one entry per FEC set in block order: which pieces made up the block, how each arrived, and when. Summed, the counts may reconcile with the block-level shred counts on this row, except in the case of equivocation where FEC sets may be shared between versions of the slot. Best-effort for pruned incomplete blocks: empty does not mean the block had no FEC sets, but that the FEC may have been pruned before it was able to be reported.

element.description: Reception detail for one FEC set. A zero timestamp means the stage was never reached or its stamp was unavailable.

merkle_root.description: Merkle root of the FEC set: its identity. The final FEC set's merkle root is the block id.

index.description: Index of the FEC set's first data shred within the block; FEC sets are listed in block order, so for a fully received block the indices ascend from 0 without gaps.

data_shreds_received_mask.description: Bitmap of data shreds of the FEC set received (vs recovered). Bit j set if the data shred with data index j was received.

parity_shreds_received_mask.description: Bitmap of parity shreds of the FEC set received (vs recovered). Bit j set if the parity shred with parity index j was received.

repair_shreds_received_mask.description: Bitmap of data shreds of the FEC set received via repair. Bit j set if the data shred with data index j arrived via repair.

duplicate_shred_count.description: Number of duplicate shreds received for this FEC set; best-effort given upstream deduplication.

first_shred_received_time.description: Timestamp when the first shred of this FEC set arrived at the shred tile.

completed_time.description: Timestamp when the FEC set was complete (assembled).

final_shred_source.description: The source of the final shred that completed the FEC set.

leader.description: Produced as our own leader shred.
